module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 534

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/534](https://www.erdosproblems.com/534)
- [Er73] Erdős, P., _Problems and results on combinatorial number theory_. A survey of
  combinatorial theory (Proc. Internat. Sympos., Colorado State Univ., Fort Collins, Colo., 1971)
  (1973), 117-138.
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, _A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory_. Ann. Discrete Math.
  (1980), 89-115.
- [AhKh96] Ahlswede, Rudolf and Khachatrian, Levon H., _Sets of integers with pairwise common
  divisor and a factor from a specified set of primes_. Acta Arith. (1996), 259--276.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos534

/-- A set `A ⊆ {1, …, N}` is *admissible* if it contains `N` and any two distinct elements
of `A` have a common factor. -/
def IsAdmissible (N : ℕ) (A : Finset ℕ) : Prop :=
  A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N ∧ N ∈ A ∧ (A : Set ℕ).Pairwise fun a b ↦ 1 < Nat.gcd a b

/-- The largest size of an admissible subset of `{1, …, N}`. -/
noncomputable def maxCard (N : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sSup {n | ∃ A : Finset ℕ, IsAdmissible N A ∧ A.card = n}

/-- The prime factors `q₁ < ⋯ < qⱼ` of `N` which are at most `q`. -/
def primePrefix (N q : ℕ) : Finset ℕ := N.primeFactors.filter (· ≤ q)

/-- The Ahlswede–Khachatrian set associated to a prime factor `q` of `N`: those integers in
`[1, N]` which are a multiple of at least one of `2 q₁, …, 2 qⱼ, q₁ ⋯ qⱼ`, where
`q₁ < ⋯ < qⱼ = q` are the prime factors of `N` which are at most `q`. -/
def ahlswedeKhachatrian (N q : ℕ) : Finset ℕ :=
  (Finset.Icc 1 N).filter fun m ↦
    (∏ p ∈ primePrefix N q, p) ∣ m ∨ ∃ p ∈ primePrefix N q, 2 * p ∣ m

/--
What is the largest possible subset $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ which contains $N$ such that
$\mathrm{gcd}(a,b)>1$ for all $a\neq b\in A$?

Erdős conjectured that if $N=q_1^{k_1}\cdots q_r^{k_r}$ (where $q_1<\cdots <q_r$ are distinct
primes) then the maximum is achieved by, for some $1\leq j\leq r$, those integers in $[1,N]$
which are a multiple of at least one of $\{2q_1,\ldots,2q_j,q_1\cdots q_j\}$.

This conjecture was proved by Ahlswede and Khachatrian [AhKh96].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos534.lean#L39"]
theorem erdos_534 (N : ℕ) (hN : 2 ≤ N) :
    ∃ q ∈ N.primeFactors, IsAdmissible N (ahlswedeKhachatrian N q) ∧
      maxCard N = (ahlswedeKhachatrian N q).card := by
  sorry

end Erdos534

reformulations.difference: The Lean asserts ∃ q ∈ N.primeFactors such that the AK set for q is admissible and maxCard N (an sSup over cardinalities of admissible Finsets, which may contain 1) equals its cardinality. Ahlswede–Khachatrian's Conjecture 1/Theorem 1 instead states g(n) = max_{1≤j≤r} |M(2q_1,…,2q_j,q_1⋯q_j) ∩ [1,n]|, where g(n) is the maximal k with 1 < a_1 < … < a_k = n and pairwise (a_i,a_j) ≠ 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: (1) Every AK set is admissible: N is divisible by q_1⋯q_j, and any two members share q (both multiples of the prefix product), 2 (both multiples of some 2p), or p (one of each kind). So |E_j| ≤ g(N) for all j, and '∃ j, g(N) = |E_j|' is equivalent to 'g(N) = max_j |E_j|'. (2) The set of admissible cardinalities is nonempty ({N}) and bounded by N, so sSup is the attained maximum. (3) For N ≥ 2, 1 cannot lie in an admissible A containing N, since gcd(1,N) = 1; so allowing 1 ∈ A changes nothing. Proved in Lean in a scratch file importing the module: equivalence with `maxCard N = N.primeFactors.sup (fun q => (ahlswedeKhachatrian N q).card)` for N ≥ 2, admissibility of every AK set, and equivalence with the linked proof's form `∀ A, IsAdmissible N A → A.card ≤ (ahlswedeKhachatrian N q).card`.

review.notes:
Checks performed:
(a) Source text. erdosproblems.com/534's refined conjecture and Ahlswede–Khachatrian's Conjecture 1 (proved as Theorem 1; its hypothesis n ≥ ∏q_i holds automatically for n = N) match the Lean statement and docstrings.
(b) Lean scratch proofs. AK sets are always admissible. The file's statement is equivalent to g(N) = max_j |E_j|, and to the linked proof's form.
(c) Brute-force max-clique computation. g(N) equals the best AK set size for all 2 ≤ N ≤ 130 and for N ∈ {105, 165, 195, 231, 255, 273, 285}. The Lean AK sizes match OEIS A387543 for n ≤ 75, give 256 at N = 2431 (q = 17, j = 3; OEIS a(2431) = 256), give two maxima of 391 at N = 4301 (q = 11 and q = 23, as OEIS notes), and give 1063 at N = 5005 (j = 4, matching AhKh96 §6).
(d) formal_proof. The linked plby/lean-proofs file exists at the pinned commit, with the theorem at line 39. Its definitions (Admissible, primePrefix, candidate) are identical to the file's. The development contains no sorry, axiom or native_decide. I compiled the whole development under this repo's toolchain (v4.33.1) in /workspace/review. From Erdos534.erdos_534 I derived the file's exact statement, with the definitions copied verbatim into a separate namespace. #print axioms gives only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].
The original [Er73]/[Er80] wordings could not be read (the Erdős-archive PDFs are scans without a text layer). This does not affect the verdict: the formalized claim is the refined conjecture recorded in AhKh96, which also quotes the [Er80] form of the problem.
